Architecture checks must exercise the ownership-only APIs and reject hashing capabilities in trusted transport/spill paths, including helpers under different names. Tests retain count/order/source/lifecycle and real I/O-failure coverage, plus unchanged scientific application comparisons. Banning the word "seal" is not a sufficient regression check.

Reintroduction requires an explicit architectural decision and owner approval, with a concrete failure model and measured CPU, memory, I/O and end-to-end cost.

docs.title: ADR-0016: Imaging foundation
docs.text:
Status: accepted Date: 2026-10-07 Truth class: normative Supersedes: 0010; the "Migration" section and the attestation wording of 0009; the joint continuum-plus-line decision of 0011 Superseded by:

Amended: 2026-10-25, on owner direction: every imaging crate may depend on the definitional crates (decision 10).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Programme #486 delivered cube, MFS, Clark, multi-worker and Metal imaging as several parallel routes: four CPU gridding drivers, two Metal drivers, closed enums selecting gridders, a 20k-line replay cache standing in for re-reading the MeasurementSet, and a runtime whose receipts, execution DAG, resource topology and identity hashing were almost entirely write-only. W-projection, AW-projection and mosaic could not reach the fast cube path or Metal. The programme's own process machinery (a migration matrix, a 3,578-line checker hashing Rust function bodies, per-ticket contract revisions) would resist any consolidation. The owner reviewed this state on 2026-10-07 and approved the plan in docs/imaging-architecture/imaging-foundation-plan-20261007.md.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
CASA-RS imaging is one measurement operator, one major-cycle pass, one deconvolution driver and one execution model. The plan document is the normative design; this ADR records the decisions that supersede earlier ADRs.

  1. One operator. casa-imaging-operator owns Placement/SampleBlock records, a ConvolutionFunctionSet trait with exactly four implementations (standard spheroidal, W-planes, AW catalog, mosaic PB), a GridBackend trait with exactly two implementations (CPU, Metal), GridAccumulator, MeasurementOperator and WeightingGeneration. Standard, W, AW, mosaic, MT-MFS, cube and MFS imaging are parameterisations of these types. Paired forward/adjoint choices (kernel set, conjugation, Mueller routing, phase gradient, phase-centre phasor, channel and polarisation maps, Taylor factors) live in the kernel contract of plan section 5.3.
  2. One pass. Every major cycle re-traverses the selected MeasurementSet through MajorCyclePass and grids residual samples. No replay cache of visibility-independent factors is retained; a bounded tap-plan cache may be added later only as a measured execution strategy over the same operator.
  3. One driver. casa-imaging-deconvolution owns the minor-cycle driver, the controller (thresholds, cycleniter, convergence and divergence rules) and a Solver trait with Hogbom, Clark, multiscale and Taylor implementations.
  4. Runtime core. Resource handling is HostResources, a ResourcePolicy, one admit() per phase returning an RAII reservation, a sequential phase list with a cancel token, the Metal execution state and the bounded worker team. There are no execution receipts, execution DAG, lease epochs, logical/physical slot ledgers, cost-model profiles, adaptation transitions or plan identities. The only runtime record is an O(1)-per-phase run summary. ADR-0010 is superseded in full.
  5. No identity hashing. Compiled problems, plans, products and selections are compared directly or by ownership. No identity is persisted; an AW convolution-function cache is reused by its cell layout (decision 7). ADR-0014 and ADR-0015 remain in force and are extended to plans and receipts. Nothing of casa-rs's is persisted in a MeasurementSet: no keywords, generations, identities or marker files. Imaging opens a MeasurementSet as CASA writes it (owner direction 2026-10-09, which amends ADR-0008).
  6. Grid precision. Metal accumulates in f32; CPU defaults to f64 and offers f32 as a user-selectable request field. Acceptance is the 1e-3 normalised tolerance of the owner's 2026-09-24 direction, not bitwise agreement.
  7. AW cache. CASA CF images are read directly (headers at open, cells on demand into a bounded in-memory LRU). Native EVLA generation writes CASA-format CF images. There is no private content-addressed store, manifest, payload hash or eviction ledger.
  8. Request layer. One ImagingRequest struct defaulted and validated from the provider-contracts catalog; one CompiledProblem; one availability gate. Capabilities that are rejected are not in the catalog.
  9. Diagnostics. Library crates read no environment variables and emit no eprintln!; diagnostic switches are request fields; emission is tracing.
  10. Crates. casa-imaging-model, casa-imaging-operator, casa-imaging-deconvolution, casa-imaging-products, casa-imaging-runtime, casa-imaging-metal (macOS), and casa-imaging-application. casa-imaging-reconstruction is deleted when empty. Dependency direction is enforced by scripts/check-imaging-dependencies.py over cargo metadata. Every crate the policy covers, the model included, may depend on the definitional crates: crates that define values, units, quanta, measures and coordinate systems and the pure functions on them, do no file, network, process or environment I/O, start no threads, use no device, and depend on no workspace crate but one another. They are casa-values, casa-types and casa-coordinates; beyond them the model has no workspace dependencies. The policy names the definitional crates and lists each crate's other workspace dependencies exactly. Adding a crate to the definitional set widens what every layer may use, so it is the owner's decision, recorded on its pull request; the checks above then apply to it. (Amended 2026-10-25 on owner direction: with no workspace dependencies at all, the model could not share the workspace's correlation, measure and coordinate vocabulary and kept private copies of it, such as CorrelationType, DirectionFrame, FrequencyFrame and Epoch.)
  11. Joint continuum-plus-line reconstruction is removed from the code. ADR-0011's sequential continuum subtraction remains; its joint-basis decision is superseded and may be re-proposed as a separate ADR with its own scientific contract.
  12. Process. The migration matrix, contract revisions, evidence registries and programme-specific closure rules are retired. Tickets IF-0 to IF-11 under issue #648 are the work record; review gates R1 to R4 in plan section 9.3 are the only review checkpoints; the anti-slop rules in plan section 10 are review criteria for every ticket.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - One place for each scientific choice; W, AW and mosaic reach every backend and the cube streaming path. - About 130k lines of parallel routes and write-only bookkeeping removed; target under 70k non-test imaging lines. - Tests become laws and tolerances rather than fixture expectations.

Negative: - Later major cycles re-read the MeasurementSet; the performance pass must show this is within the measured checkpoints or add a bounded cache. - Between tickets some capabilities are temporarily unavailable (Metal between IF-2 and IF-4; W/AW/mosaic between IF-2 and IF-3). They fail typed. - Receipts consumed by the manual intermediate_profile_evidence.py tool are replaced by the run summary.

Neutral / tradeoffs: - Metal f32 accumulation differs from CPU f64 within tolerance; this is a precision choice, not a correctness gap.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
1. Keep the replay cache as the default residual path. Rejected: it is not scientifically required, its scratch footprint exceeds the input, and it duplicates the operator in a second record-based implementation.
  2. Keep ADR-0010's resource authority and trim it. Rejected: its admission decisions reduce to one arithmetic formula, and every other structure was write-only.
  3. Keep the architecture checker and update its ratchets per commit. Rejected: it enforced programme process, not architecture.
  4. (Amendment of 2026-10-25.) Keep the model free of workspace dependencies and convert between vocabularies at the application, or admit each definitional dependency into each crate's exact set. Rejected: the first keeps two types for one meaning; the second makes every use of a unit or measure a policy edit while guarding nothing, since a definitional crate brings in no persistence, I/O or device. casa-numerics and casa-fft are algorithms rather than definitions and stay listed where used.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: This decision is enforced by: - tests: T0 operator laws and T1 end-to-end capability tests (plan section 7) - lint/import/dependency rules: scripts/check-imaging-dependencies.py (crate edges, definitional crates closed and free of I/O, device APIs only in casa-imaging-metal, no std::env or eprintln! in library crates, no content hashing in imaging crates) - CI checks: just arch-check - review trigger: plan section 10 rules at every IF ticket review; gates R1–R4

docs.title: ADR-0017: Python and headless task providers are the product surface
docs.text: Status: accepted Date: 2026-10-20 Truth class: normative Supersedes: 0005; 0007; the stateful-session provider and session-surface parts of 0003 and 0006 Superseded by:

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
From May to October 2026 casa-rs carried several interactive surfaces beside its Python package and command-line tasks: a ratatui terminal launcher with image and table browsers (casars), a native macOS SwiftUI workbench (apps/casars-mac, ADR-0005), a scientific-notebook and AI-assistant program (casa-notebook, ADR-0007), JSONL browser-session providers (imexplore --session, tablebrowser) with their own parameter surfaces, and Rust-side plot rasterisation (PNG/PDF through plotters, image and printpdf). The experiments showed that one computational codebase and one task/parameter contract can serve several frontends, but each frontend added code, tests, CI time (a macOS GUI gate on every pull request) and support crates that competed with the scientific work.

The project's direction is a Python package that mirrors CASA's Python interfaces (casatasks-style task calls and ia/tb-style tools) so casa-rs can replace CASA in existing scripts. Interactive inspection and plotting are better served by Python tools (NumPy, Matplotlib, Jupyter) than by project-owned GUIs.

The last state of the interactive surfaces is preserved at the tag ui-experiments-2026-10-20 (commit 42ba2012).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. The product surfaces are the Python package (casars), the headless task host casars (casars run and casars params), and the task-provider executables listed in the application catalog.
  2. casa-rs has no terminal UI, native GUI, notebook or assistant program, interactive browser sessions, or Rust-side plot rasterisation. Every parameter surface is a one-shot task; SurfaceKind and SurfaceDefinition keep a single task variant so the serialized contracts keep their shape.
  3. Plots are typed data. Rust builds plot documents and text point manifests (msexplore/plotms --plot-format txt); Python renders them with Matplotlib (casars.data.plot_matplotlib, casars.imexplore).
  4. casars-frontend-services is the UniFFI service layer of the Python package only. It exports what casars.parameters, casars.tasks and casars.data call, and nothing for other frontends.
  5. New interactive surfaces, if ever wanted again, start from a new ADR rather than from the retired code.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - The workspace loses the terminal, GUI, notebook, browser-protocol and rasterisation crates and dependencies (ratatui*, crossterm, plotters, image, printpdf, rusqlite, UniFFI Swift bindings and others). - CI no longer needs a macOS GUI job; the required checks are lint_test, python_package and docs. - Contract and runtime code no longer carries session-only branches.

Negative: - There is no point-and-click inspection; users inspect data from Python. - msexplore/plotms no longer write PNG or PDF files.

Neutral / tradeoffs: - Catalog presentation fields (show_in_tui, show_in_swift, shell_kind, interaction) and the provider CLI parser schema (casa_ms::presentation::UiCommandSchema) remain until the CASA-shaped Python work reshapes them.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
1. Keep the Swift GUI as the primary surface: rejected; Python reaches the intended users and existing CASA scripts directly.
  2. Keep the TUI as a lightweight viewer: rejected; it duplicated the GUI's browsing model and carried terminal-graphics dependencies for little gain.
  3. Keep the code dormant behind feature flags: rejected; dormant code still costs build time, review and maintenance, and the tag preserves it.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: This decision is enforced by: - tests: crates/casars/tests/casars_cli.rs (no launcher or open command; casars run executes a provider), the provider-contract and catalog tests (27 task surfaces, no session kinds), the Python package tests; - lint/import/dependency rules: none beyond the workspace manifests; - CI checks: just quick, scripts/generate-frontend-bindings.sh --check in the python_package job, just docs-check; - review trigger: any pull request that adds a UI, rendering or session dependency or crate.

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text: Suspect drift if: - Cargo.lock gains ratatui, crossterm, plotters, image, printpdf or a UniFFI foreign-language generator other than Python; - a parameter surface or provider declares a non-task kind; - casars-frontend-services grows exports that the Python package does not call.

docs.title: ADR-0018: Rust computes; Python is the interface
docs.text: Status: accepted Date: 2026-10-20 Truth class: normative Supersedes: Superseded by:

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
ADR-0017 makes the product surface a Python package that mirrors CASA's Python interfaces: casatasks-style tasks and ia/tb-style tools. CASA puts a large share of its user-level logic in Python. Whole tasks such as simobserve, simanalyze and simalma are Python scripts over C++ tools, and helper modules such as simutil compute pointings, sensitivities and sky-model rescaling with NumPy. Copying that structure would put interpreted, GIL-bound code on the paths users time, and would split each task's behaviour between two languages with two sets of defaults and validation.

Performance is a top priority for casa-rs, and its Rust crates already own parallelism, memory budgets and casacore-compatible I/O.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Computation lives in Rust. Numerical work, data access, file formats, and the orchestration that CASA writes in Python (task scripts and helpers such as simutil) are implemented in Rust crates. When CASA implements a task or tool in Python, casa-rs reads that Python as the specification and ports its semantics to Rust, as it does for C++.
  2. Python is an interface. The casars package:
  3. presents CASA's module, function and method names, signatures and return shapes;
  4. converts arguments and results: Python scalars, lists and dicts, and NumPy arrays as an exchange format;
  5. maps errors to Python exceptions;
  6. starts the work.

It contains no loops over rows, pixels or channels, no numerical algorithms and no file-format code. 3. One source of defaults and validation. Defaults, value normalization and validation come from Rust-owned definitions, for tools as well as tasks. For tasks that is the parameter contract of ADR-0006. The Python layer keeps no second copy. 4. Plot rendering stays in Python, under ADR-0017 item 3. Python may turn Rust-built plot documents into Matplotlib figures, including deriving the coordinate metadata that Matplotlib and Astropy need. This is the only computation the Python layer performs. 5. Rust APIs stay idiomatic (ADR-0002). CASA's call shapes exist only in the Python layer, which maps them onto Rust APIs. Rust crates do not grow CASA-shaped wrappers for the binding's convenience. 6. Rust owns parallelism, and long calls release the GIL. - Python never divides work into chunks, processes or threads for speed. - A Rust call that can run for more than a moment releases the GIL, so other Python threads, such as a notebook kernel's event loop, keep running. - The existing casars._core Image and Table bindings do not release it yet; #839 tracks that fix. New bindings release it from the start.

This decision does not fix the binding mechanism for each surface. Today: - tasks run through the headless task host (casars run); - stateful tools are expected to be in-process objects in the casars._core extension, like casars.data.Image and casars.data.Table; - ADR-0017 item 4 limits the UniFFI layer to what the Python package calls.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - Each behaviour has one implementation, in the language that sets its speed. - CASA scripts run at casa-rs speed without Python-level hot loops. - Tasks and the tools they are built on share Rust code, so they cannot drift apart. - Rust callers get the full functionality without Python.

Negative: - Porting CASA's Python-level logic, such as task scripts and simutil, takes more work than wrapping or copying it. - Each new tool needs Rust bindings for its methods; it cannot start as a quick Python prototype that ships. - Quirks in CASA's Python logic must be reproduced on purpose in Rust, or recorded as divergences in docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md.

Neutral / tradeoffs: - NumPy remains a dependency of the Python package, for array exchange rather than computation. - Exploratory Python may be used during development to understand CASA behaviour, but it does not ship.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
1. Mirror CASA's split, porting its Python task scripts and helpers as Python over Rust primitives. Rejected: hot paths would run in the interpreter, and behaviour would be split across two languages.
  2. Allow NumPy computation in Python where it is "fast enough". Rejected: the boundary would erode case by case, and NumPy code is single-threaded and allocates on every operation.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: This decision is enforced by: - tests: Python tests exercise behaviour through the Rust implementation; parity tests compare it with CASA - lint/import/dependency rules: none automatic - CI checks: none specific; the existing python_package job runs the Python tests - review trigger: a change under crates/casars-python/python/casars that does any of the following: - computes on data; - parses a file format; - loops over rows, pixels or channels; - keeps its own default or validation; - splits work for parallelism. - none / guidance only:

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text: Suspect drift if: - a casars module other than plot rendering does arithmetic on NumPy arrays or iterates over data - a Python default or validation rule duplicates, or disagrees with, the Rust definition - a CASA task is implemented by porting its Python script into the casars package - a Rust crate gains an API whose only purpose is to mimic a CASA call shape

docs.title: ADR-0019: CASA tools are Rust-declared pyo3 objects in casars.tools
docs.text: Status: accepted Date: 2026-10-20 Truth class: normative Supersedes: Superseded by:

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
ADR-0017 makes a Python package that mirrors CASA's Python interfaces the product surface. ADR-0018 puts all computation in Rust, but leaves open how each surface binds to Rust. Tasks already have a mechanism: the parameter contract and casars run. CASA tools do not yet. The simulation programme brings the first one, the simulator (sm), and ia, tb, ms, cl and others will follow. Every later tool reuses whatever pattern the first one sets.

CASA scripts construct tools as objects, for example from casatools import simulator; sm = simulator(), and then call methods with CASA's parameter names. The defaults those calls see are the installed Python binding's, not the text in the tool's XML. In particular, parameters of "any" type default to [], which the C++ reads as 0 before applying its own fallbacks.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Namespace.
  2. CASA tool classes live in casars.tools, under casatools' class names: simulator, and later image, table, measurementset, componentlist and the rest.
  3. Tasks stay in casars.tasks.
  4. A CASA script changes only its imports.
  5. casa-rs ships no casatools or casatasks alias packages, because they would shadow a real CASA installation.
  6. Each tool is a pyo3 class in the casars._core extension, exposed directly; the Python package adds only the module path.
  7. Methods and parameters have CASA's names, and return what CASA's return.
  8. Signatures and defaults are declared in Rust (pyo3 signature). They reproduce the installed CASA binding's effective defaults, not the XML text, where the two differ.
  9. The object-surface schema bundle describes each method from the same Rust types.
  10. Controls CASA lacks are keyword-only constructor arguments with Rust-owned defaults: the memory budget, the backend (auto, cpu, metal) and the worker count. No tool reads environment variables (ADR-0016).
  11. Tools release the GIL. Tool state is Send, and classes are not unsendable. Every method that touches the disk, copies array data or computes releases the GIL. The existing casars.data Image and Table bindings move to this rule under #839.
  12. Tools are thin over idiomatic Rust APIs (ADR-0002, ADR-0018 item 5).
  13. The pyo3 layer maps CASA's argument conventions (quantity strings, measures records, scalar-or-list arguments) onto Rust types.
  14. Those conversions are shared by every tool, not written once per tool.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - Every tool follows one pattern, so a CASA script works the same way across tools. - Signatures and defaults have one Rust-owned source, which tests can compare against CASA's installed binding. - Long calls do not freeze notebooks or other Python threads.

Negative: - Copying CASA's binding defaults exactly, including their quirks, takes care, and each one must be checked against an installed CASA. - Shared state behind a Send boundary makes the tool code more complex than thread-pinned objects.

Neutral / tradeoffs: - casars.data.Image and casars.data.Table stay until CASA-shaped image and table tools arrive. Whether casars.data remains after that is decided then. - Tools bypass the task parameter contract and Last state, as CASA's tools do.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
1. Python wrapper classes over Rust primitives. Rejected: defaults and argument handling would live in Python, against ADR-0018.
  2. UniFFI objects in casars-frontend-services. Rejected: there is no precedent, and the pyo3 Image and Table classes already work in-process with NumPy.
  3. casatools and casatasks alias packages. Rejected: they would shadow a real CASA installation in the same environment.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: This decision is enforced by: - tests: each tool's Python tests construct it from casars.tools. With the first tool (simulation Phase 1c), a test compares every method's signature and defaults against the installed CASA binding when CASA is available. - lint/import/dependency rules: none automatic - CI checks: the existing python_package job - review trigger: - a tool written as a Python class; - a default declared in Python; - a tool reading environment variables; - an unsendable tool class; - a casatools or casatasks package. - none / guidance only:

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text: Suspect drift if: - a tool's method signature or default differs from CASA's installed binding without a recorded divergence - per-tool code re-implements quantity, measures or list conversion - a long tool call holds the GIL

docs.title: AW-projection prior art: what made the pre-refactor VLASS rows fast, and what happened to it
docs.text:
Truth class: non-normative primary-source research Date: 2026-10-16 Work issue: #449 (the 10x programme)

Research notes, 2026-10-16. A read-only study of the casa-rs repository at 6a9e83f36b and its GitHub issues. Nothing was built or run.

The figures in section 4 are the study's own estimates, not measurements. The open owner decisions this raises are recorded on #449: whether the recovery contract's landmarks are retired, and how ADR-0016 decision 2 treats a tap-plan cache.

Abbreviations: - HP is the historical VLASS plan docs/tutorial-parity/vlass-imaging-optimization-plan.md as it stood at 873776457e^. It is 8,341 lines and was deleted by 873776457e on 2026-08-13. Line numbers below refer to that version. - RC is docs/tutorial-parity/vlass-imaging-recovery-contract.md at HEAD. - FP is docs/imaging-architecture/imaging-foundation-plan-20261007.md at HEAD. - L is crates/casa-imaging/src/lib.rs at d2d0c0dad5, the last August production commit before the main merge. The crate is 86,874 lines; the same symbols are still present in 96,376 lines at the main merge ba0354ef93.

docs.title: 0. The most important finding: two deletions, not one
docs.text:
The fast VLASS mechanisms were not removed by the imaging-foundation refactor.

Lineage. These are verified with git merge-base --is-ancestor:

41caf8cd0a (07-29 work, pushed 08-02) → 8667b5760d (casa-c) → 388161fd29 → f2abbb98bd → 4d787cb1fb (casa-d checkpoint) → d2d0c0dad5 → ba0354ef93 (main merge, 2026-08-13).

First deletion: the August ADR-0009 cutover. - Two commits deleted the whole legacy casa-imaging crate (96,750 lines) and the casars-imager monolith (82,961 lines): - fff9c2d553, "complete native continuum cutover", 2026-08-25; - 27b9b602fe, "complete final-owner cutover", 2026-08-25. - The programme behind them was the #486 imaging-architecture programme, with its migration matrix and "transfer ratchet". - At that cutover the migration matrix marked AW as "typed unavailable boundary; no production implementation". AW was rebuilt later in T50–T53 (#536–#539). The matrix is at 27b9b602fe:resources/imaging-architecture/migration-matrix.json. - What went with the crate: - the frozen-base image-response cache; - the compact replay cache; - Metal resident/global/grouped replay; - the sparse MT-MFS right-hand side (RHS); - radix MADFM; - the NEON 2×2 sparse initial grid; - compensated Metal AW gridding. - git log -S'struct AwProjectImageResponseCache' shows the struct was added by 41caf8cd0a and removed by 27b9b602fe.

What #486 re-implemented. - A generic gridded-normal replay: - crates/casa-imaging-reconstruction/src/gridded_normal_operator.rs, added by 712b399f8e (2026-08-24) and e413729fa8 (2026-08-28); - 40-byte scalar records and 96-byte AW records (AW_GRIDDED_NORMAL_OPERATOR_RECORD_BYTES, e714fd2339 version, around line 85); - crates/casa-imaging-runtime/src/complete_data_operator.rs. - complete_data_operator/metal_normal.rs (565b79a54d, 2026-10-04, standard MFS).

Second deletion: IF-2 under D1. - e7d29c8e5b (IF-2, 2026-10-07, "run every request through the major-cycle pass and delete the old drivers") deleted the gridded-normal replay and metal_normal.rs. - reconstruction/src/image_response.rs at e714fd2339 is not the response cache. It is the flat-noise/flat-sky PB normalisation (MinorCycleImageResponse). It moved to products in e83759240d.

When the fast path was last production. - The August production freeze (PR #464, merged 2026-08-13) had already chosen "role-segmented source-major Metal initial gridding with CPU residual refresh" for full geometry. - The VLASS recovery retrospective (4a29cc1d52:docs/tutorial-parity/vlass-imaging-recovery-retrospective.md) says the CPU residual backend "produced a scientifically accepted result after compressed and Metal-residual candidates failed". - The accepted 12,150² all-63-field, 16-SPW clean took about 40,412 s against CASA-B's 82,351.8 s, about 2.0×. The no-new-swap guard was waived (PR #464; TESTING.md at 6ce6fad837).

No pre-IF build ever ran the #625 row (63 fields, 16 SPWs, 4096², niter 2000) for time. - #625 was queued and never activated. - An August cleaned 4096²/16-SPW/63-field run (r22) passed science (PR #464), but no wall time is recorded in the repository, PR #464 or the #454 comments. - The run logs (r22, v24, the 28.65 s log, casa-c) are not available: - /Volumes/GLENDENNING/casa-rs-vlass/issue-446/ now holds only data and masks; - the NAS preservation copy /Volumes/home/casa-rs-glendenning-preserve/GLENDENNING/casa-rs-vlass/issue-446/ holds only input tars (casa-reduced-clean, cf-cache*, data*, masks, recovery-references, t51…), no receipts/runs or recovery-candidates. - Everything below therefore rests on repository and issue text.

Governance finding. - RC lines 530–569 still require that the single-field landmarks be preserved, and say a landmark capability may leave the lineage only when generalised, superseded on the same landmark, or "explicitly retired by Brian" (RC:563–568). - The capability was deleted twice: at the August cutover and by IF-2. - I found no retirement record in: - #445, #454, #486 or #487 (bodies and comments, searched for landmark, 28.65, retire, response cache and preservation); - the cutover migration matrix; - HEAD docs. - RC at HEAD is therefore stale against the code.

docs.text:
Build. - The commit is not recorded; the contract binds only the run log's SHA-256 (f07d3b87…). - The code was squashed into 41caf8cd0a (author date 2026-07-29, committed 2026-08-02). Its message reads "improving the same-host exact control from 143.15s to 28.65s". - Run log: 20260729-vlass-clean4096-4spw-n2000-image-response-radix-madfm-v4.log (HP:3315–3409).

Run configuration. - Metal AW (--standard-mfs-acceleration metal), grid threads 2, FFTW f64 with 8 threads. - Env flags IMAGE_RESPONSE_CACHE, MODEL_DELTA_CENSUS, RADIX_MADFM, CACHE_REFRESHED_NSIGMA, SPARSE_MASK_PEAK_SEARCH, PARALLEL_MODEL_TERM_FFT, SPARSE_MODEL_PREP. Mechanism. The frozen-base image response (HP:3315–3358). - Model-delta census: 167 late major cycles update only pixel (581, 2143). - After two stable cycles, one exact refresh is run. A central ±0.125 response is then measured for each input Taylor term with the exact operator (4 extra exact applications). - Later residuals are synthesised as base − Δm·H·e_p. The cache is invalidated on any new delta position, and the final refresh is always exact. - The successor hybrid run (29.43 s) did 11 exact refreshes over 171 major cycles (HP:7088–7092). - CASA did 171 full degrid/grid major cycles (HP:3046–3049).

Stages.

Stage Seconds Core 24.81 Major refresh 11.15 Controller 4.57 Sparse minor 2.33 Initial PSF grid 3.55 Model FFT 2.07 Residual degrid/grid 5.59 Residual FFT 2.34

Not like-for-like. 1. Different hosts and CASA versions, as far as the evidence shows. - The evidence indicates that the CASA oracle ran CASA 6.7.5.18 on the Mac mini (M2). This is an inference: GLENDENNING is an external SSD, so a GLENDENNING path alone does not prove the laptop. The oracle script 873776457e^:tools/perf/imager/experiments/vlass_reduced_casa_clean_4096_four_spw.py writes to /Volumes/Extra Storage (not encrypted)/… with "casa_version": "6.7.5.18". - Its products were later "copied from the Mac mini to GLENDENNING" (HP:5159). - casa-rs's 28.65 s ran on the M4 laptop (GLENDENNING paths; HP:3317 "same-host" refers to the casa-rs control only). - The same-host figure is the c238 seed on the mini: 46.14 s with 2,000 components and 171 cycles, using the same four-SPW runner SHA 1a9ba23a…. That is 78.7×. Source: tools/perf/imager/vlass_recovery_salvage_catalog.json. 2. Compared only with the casa-rs control. - The 28.65 s run was compared with the exact casa-rs control, not with CASA; its "promotion" was retracted on 2026-07-30 (HP:3396–3404, 5151–5221). - The V6 29.82 s rerun against CASA was 5.7 ppm, with 16 alpha pixels. - The scientific-floor pass is the 29.43 s hybrid run (HP:7418–7499; receipt 20260731-vlass-4096-4spw-scientific-floor-v2.json). 3. Experimental and single-position. The response cache was env-gated (L:6436) and admitted only for a single pending delta position (L:6810–6816). It never admitted the 63-field trajectory (RC:536–539; HP:7765–7775). 4. Workload otherwise the same: the same recipe, mask, products and real CLEAN from zero.

Later production rebaseline. - The grouped architecture took 38.5 s (94.3× nominal), with the ceiling at 42.35 s (owner, 2026-08-07, HP:8113–8117). - That run then failed science: its CF support was cropped at 1e-6 energy, giving NRMSE 0.05–0.15 (HP:8131–8147). - The exact-support rerun took 55.40 s (65.6× nominal) and passed science (HP:8160–8197).

docs.title: 2. Mechanisms that made those rows fast
docs.text:
# Mechanism Code at d2d0c0dad5 (L unless noted) Doc text Used by M1 Frozen-base image response (exact columns H·e_p for one pixel, per Taylor input×output term pair; 4×N²×f64 = 512 MiB at 4096²) AwProjectImageResponseCache L:5044; from_central_calibrations L:5061; calibration and activation L:6810–6898; final synthesis L:6949; env CASA_RS_EXPERIMENTAL_AWPROJECT_IMAGE_RESPONSE_CACHE L:6436 HP:3315–3358; RC:536–539, 573–585 28.65 / 29.43 s (single field); inert on 63 fields M2 Compact source-order replay cache: per-sample plans and packed AW tap bundles retained across majors AwProjectCompactReplayCache L:10429; AwProjectCompactReplayWindow L:10295; replay_awproject_compact_window L:35184 HP:3107–3140 (residual refresh 7.86 → 2.10 s); HP:3076–3088 (tap rematerialisation 758 s, CF loads 585.5 s, 48 hits in 143,926 loads) all clean rows M3 Metal resident replay program: per-sample observed visibilities, prediction plans, interned kernels and phases; separable X/Y phase atlas. The MS is not touched in residual majors; residual = V − A·m per sample on the GPU AwProjectMetalResidentProgram L:12223; AwProjectMetalPredictionSample L:11557 (holds first/second_observed_re/im); build_awproject_metal_global_replay_program L:26572; replay_awproject_metal_global_program L:34351 RC:612–622; HP:7832–7865 (17.69 → 5.22 GB) casa-d 257.4 s; landmarks M4 Grouped AOT tile replay: exact-support compiler, sorted groups, persistent integrity-checked spill, next-use-aware residency compile_awproject_metal_aot_grouped_tile L:24333; refresh_awproject_metal_aot_grouped_tile L:24582; replay_awproject_metal_{spilled,resident}_global_programs L:34961 / 35048 RC:658–707; HP:7916–8170; PR #461 268.49 s; 55.4 / 86.6 s M5 Sparse multi-worker CPU initial grid: 192-pixel tiles, dynamic scheduler, NEON 2×2, 512 MiB tap arena AwProjectInitialGridPlan L:5749; resolved_awproject_initial_grid_plan L:5766; AwProjectNeonReplay2x2 L:15219 HP:8265–8312 casa-d initial pass, 119.7 / 132.8 s M6 Compensated Metal AW gridding: two u32 fixed-point limbs plus an f32 compensation plane, f64 readback AwProjectMetalCompensation L:14049; awproject_metal_fixed_scales L:17279 HP:302–332 casa-c; single-field initial grids M7 Mask-sparse MT-MFS RHS: 384 MiB → 110,688 B of minor-cycle state; minor cycle 1.95 s L:59640–59760, env CASA_RS_EXPERIMENTAL_MT_MFS_SPARSE_RHS; build_sparse_mtmfs_scale_search_positions L:60500 HP:3206–3293 171-cycle rows M8 Exact radix MADFM, cached refreshed n-sigma, sparse mask peak search; statistics 6.27 → 3.70 s over 171 cycles radix_madfm_f32 L:67384 HP:3352–3358 171-cycle rows M9 CF locality: group samples by RR/LL CF quartet; plus prefetch, planning workers and pack workers from the 08-04 autoresearch (08-04 commits 9254efe960, cd745127a5, 2040a07635, f2abbb98bd) HP:276–284 (5,861 → 796 CF loads) all M10 FFT details: f32 casacore-layout model FFT, parallel per-term FFTs, FFTW wisdom env PARALLEL_*_TERM_FFT HP:3120–3157, 8023–8049 landmarks

Where the wall time went. - casa-d: an initial grid of about 120 s (M5) plus about 9.5 s for each of 11 Metal residual majors (M3). - Today's CPU W1 pass is about 41 s per SPW, so a 4-SPW pass is roughly 165 s. That is an estimate scaled from #625; it has not been run. - The per-major gap is about 17×. That figure confounds three things: - GPU against CPU; - multi-threaded against W1; - precompiled per-sample programs (M2/M3) against on-the-fly preparation. - What it is not is I/O avoidance. #625's MS reads are cheap: the density-pass reads take 0.6 s (#659 comment 6207741158). - The single field's 126× came mostly from M1, which removed about 160 of 171 exact passes, together with M7, M8 and M10, which cut the per-cycle fixed costs.

docs.title: 3. Fate of each mechanism
docs.text: Mechanism August → #486 #486 → IF Stated reason M1 response cache Deleted at 27b9b602fe and never ported Not present; never discussed by name The August cutover's transfer ratchet. RC:563–568 forbade silent retirement of landmark capabilities; I found no record of an owner retirement approval for the cutover. The #659 catalogue rejects "an image-domain residual (dirty image minus gridded model)" because it "cancels nearly equal f32 grids and breaks CASA's interpolate-then-subtract order" (comment 6134710065). That is a different construction, but the same argument would be raised. M2 compact replay, M3 Metal program, M4 grouped Deleted at 27b9b602fe; its conceptual successor (a different design, not a port) was the gridded-normal replay (gridded_normal_operator*, complete_data_operator*, metal_normal.rs) Deleted by IF-2 e7d29c8e5b under D1 (FP:71–87; deletion row FP:1025). Reaffirmed at R3 ("D1's re-traversal stands, and nothing argues for a replay cache", FP:1593) and at R4 ("the MAIN-walk profile does not justify a visibility or replay cache", FP:1695). D1: "not scientifically required"; about 40 B per row-channel, an 86 GB Wave3 reservation against a 36 GB input; valid only while weighting is frozen; forms the residual as a difference of two f64 images. ADR-0016 decision 2 (lines 38–41) and alternative 1 (lines 113–115). §5.9 outcome: "a tap-plan, record or placement cache across majors was rejected by design (D1, R3)" (FP:972–976). The #648 results say it was "not measured", and give deep32 cube sizes (2.6–8.9 GB a major). The narrow part kept — WeightCache: 4 B per selected row and channel, one domain, admitted at 1/16 of free memory (crates/casa-imaging-runtime/src/pass/weights.rs:17; crates/casa-imaging-application/src/imaging/cycle.rs:770–790; #659 deviation 7) — M5 sparse CPU initial grid Deleted Superseded by Partition::regions grid strips for constant and Taylor bases (cycle.rs:869–883) plus CpuBackend's seven-tap/dense kernels One driver (D4/D5 consolidation) M6 compensated Metal AW grid Deleted Metal backend accumulates f32 with atomics (D2). The AW kernel set is refused on Metal: Unsupported::KernelSetOnMetal (crates/casa-imaging-application/src/availability.rs:32–34, 217–219); auto keeps AW on the CPU (#723, deviation 14) #653 (IF-4) open: "W, mosaic and AW wait for gate R2" M7 sparse RHS, M8 radix MADFM Deleted Not ported; the Taylor solver and PlaneStatistics are in casa-imaging-deconvolution Never production defaults (env-gated) M9 CF locality and CF cache The prepared-artifact store replaced the packed CF D3: CASA CF images in a bounded LRU (FP:108–114). Deviation 10: walk one DATA_DESCRIPTION at a time, which fixes the thrash (#625 15,498 → 4,764.57 s). Factored native generation is 10.8× faster (#648 rows 19 and 20). Owner, 2026-10-11: the cfcache is not an interop contract. Kept in spirit and improved M10 FFT — NEON FFTW; per-plane FFTs single-threaded on the team (FP:962) —

docs.title: 4. Assessment: what could come back, and what it might buy
docs.text:
Constraints throughout. - One measurement operator and one pass (ADR-0016 decisions 1 and 2). - admit() before any allocation (D5). - No env vars in library crates (D9 / ADR-0016 decision 9). - Device code only in casa-imaging-metal (ADR-0016 decision 10). - The 16 GiB native policy. - #625's own bar is serial W1. Report serial gains and parallel or GPU gains separately. - The estimates below are mine. None of them is measured.

  1. AW kernel set on Metal (#653). This is the largest lever for the casa-d/#625 shape.
  2. August data: about 9.5 s per residual major for 6.4 M samples on the M4 GPU, against an estimated 165 s at CPU W1 today.
  3. It fits the existing GridBackend/Work::NativeResidualGrid design; no ADR change is needed.
  4. Risks:
    • D2's plain f32 atomics. August needed compensated accumulation (M6), and an f32 Metal residual "failed scientific comparison decisively" at 12,150² (salvage catalog, exact-metal-direct-cf-f32-residual).
    • Wide-support atomics contention: the R2 measurement #653 asked for.
    • Host preparation becomes the bottleneck. The 08-07 initial pass spent 155 s on source preparation against 136 s on Metal.
  5. It needs T0/T1 Metal AW laws and possibly an owner refinement of D2 (compensated f32).
  6. Plausible result: residual passes at August's 65–132 s plus an initial pass at August's best extrapolated figure (about 480–530 s) give about 870–1,320 s, which is 7–10×.
  7. 10× needs the initial pass to fall well below that too, for example a Metal initial grid without the CF thrash August hit. That is unmeasured.
  8. If only the residual passes move, the cap is about 7.5× (see the budget below).
  9. Multi-worker CPU AW.
  10. This already exists through Partition::Regions. #625 was timed only at W1.
  11. It is low conflict: measure W4 and charge the per-holder CF LRU (AwCatalog::charge_bytes).
  12. Plausible: 2.5–3.5× per pass, so #625 at about 1,400–1,900 s, roughly 5–6×. It does not count toward the serial bar.
  13. A bounded tap-plan (placement) cache.
  14. What it holds: per-sample CF key, placement and pointing phasor, without taps or values.
  15. ADR-0016 decision 2 explicitly permits "a bounded tap-plan cache … as a measured execution strategy". The FP §5.9 and #648 records still list it as rejected by design, so reopening it is an owner (Ask First) decision.
  16. Size: about 25 M samples on #625 at 16–32 B is 0.4–0.8 GB. It fits WeightCache-style admission.
  17. Gain: about 10–30% per pass on the CPU. Gridding dominates, and the per-row pointing conversion is about 10 s a pass. On Metal it would be much larger, because it removes the host-preparation bottleneck.
  18. A full record or program replay (observed V plus plans, as in M3/M4).
  19. D1's three objections apply unevenly to the August per-sample design:
    • "Residual as a difference of two f64 images": this described the #486 gridded-normal operator. The August Metal program formed V − A·m per sample; AwProjectMetalPredictionSample holds the observed values (L:11557). It therefore kept CASA's interpolate-then-subtract order.
    • "Valid only while weighting is frozen": this is already accepted for WeightCache (deviation 7).
    • Memory: this depends on workload and representation. Wave3 needed 86 GB at 40 B per sample. #625 at the #486 AW record size of 96 B per row-channel would be about 4 GB (about 42 M row-channels; 25.0 M accepted samples in r22). The measured M3/M4 representations were heavier: 9.3–15.2 GB resident and 17.8–19.8 GB footprint for the 16-SPW 63-field residual (PR #461).
  20. It remains Ask First, because ADR-0016 alternative 1 rejects it, so the ADR would have to be edited.
  21. ADR-0016 decision 2 is internally in tension. It says "no replay cache of visibility-independent factors" yet allows "a bounded tap-plan cache", which is exactly a cache of visibility-independent factors. The owner should resolve that wording before item 3 or item 4 is attempted.
  22. Spilled replay was slower: 14.3 GB reread a refresh made it 2× slower than resident (HP:8000–8006).
  23. Worth it only after item 1, and only if host preparation then dominates.
  24. The frozen-base response (M1), generalised to a bounded set of delta positions with exact shadow cycles and fallback (RC:570–585; HP:3405–3414 oracle requirements: dyadic calibration, a held-out exact shadow cycle, coefficient trust regions, decision-margin certificates, exact fallback).
  25. It is not named in D1, and it is mathematically exact for the linear H up to rounding.
  26. It lives in the runtime's major/minor loop, and calls run_major_cycle for the calibration columns.
  27. Cost: 512 MiB per position at 4096² and about 4.4 GiB at 12,150², so only a few positions can be admitted.
  28. Buys a lot on many-cycle single-field rows: 171 → 11 exact passes. Little on #625 (7 majors) or casa-d (11 majors), whose model delta is not single-position.
  29. It needs owner sign-off against the #659 "image-domain residual" rejection.
  30. Sparse MT-MFS RHS (M7), radix MADFM and cached n-sigma (M8).
  31. These are solver-internal (Solver::State, PlaneStatistics) with no architectural conflict.
  32. They matter only on 171-cycle rows, worth seconds per cycle; they are negligible on #625.
  33. M5 and M10. Today's Regions partition plus NEON FFTW cover most of them. Parallel per-term FFTs are a small fixed-cost win on many-cycle rows.

The 10× budget for #625, using 16-SPW data where it exists: - 10× on #625 is about 907 s in total. Today: initial pass 603 s plus six residual passes of 651–719 s, all at CPU W1. - Initial grid. - The best August initial grid was the multi-worker sparse CPU path, 120–133 s at 4 SPWs on 63 fields. - Scaled by SPW count to 16 SPWs, that is about 480–530 s. This is an estimate: the per-SPW cost was roughly constant today, 41 s per SPW per pass. - The 16-SPW single-field v59 initial grid was 60.5 s, but that is 1/63 of the rows. - Residual passes. The only 16-SPW all-field residual figures are 132.34 s (incumbent) and 65.17 s (grouped). Both stop before FFT and normalisation. - Total. About 480–530 + 6 × (65–132) ≈ 870–1,320 s. The best August mechanisms therefore extrapolate to roughly the 10× line, or short of it, on #625. They were never run there, and the resident replay footprint is 17.8–19.8 GB. - The initial grid is as large a lever as the residual. Today's 603 s initial pass alone uses two-thirds of the 907 s budget. Accelerating only the residual majors, to about 100 s each, caps #625 near 9,074 / (603 + 600) ≈ 7.5×.

No row passes 10× on the serial CPU alone. The single-field 4-SPW row is likely bound by its roughly 172 passes of FFT and normalisation fixed cost. It has not been measured on today's build, and its CASA time is the mini's.

docs.title: CASA, Obit and LibRA FFT implementation notes
docs.text: Truth class: non-normative primary-source research Last reality check: 2026-09-26 Verification: local source inspection; no new benchmark or implementation

docs.title: Finding
docs.text:
All three inspected CPU imaging implementations delegate FFT arithmetic to FFTW. Their adapters, storage choices and memory traffic differ. LibRA's HPG backend additionally delegates GPU FFTs to NVIDIA cuFFT, not Metal. This is source evidence, not proof of the backend or thread count of every distributed binary or a prediction of casa-rs speedup.

Implementation path Library and calls Layout and surrounding work CASA standard GridFT2 FFT2D::c2cFFT -> doFFT -> rank-2 fftw[f]_plan_dft and fftw[f]_execute_dft Full complex plane, in-place; forward/backward plans retained by the adapter. Explicit image centering and inverse normalization remain. CASA Clark convolution LatConvEquation -> LatticeConvolver<Float> -> LatticeFFT -> FFTServer -> FFTW Real/half-complex convolution; lattice axis traversal and FFTServer work-buffer copies remain. Not uniformly a direct rank-2 call. Obit base CPU imaging ObitUVGridFFT2Im[Par] -> ObitFFTC2R -> fftwf_execute_dft_c2r Single-precision half-complex grid to real image; complete 2D FFTW plans, retained image/beam plan objects, followed by centering and normalization/correction. LibRA standard GridFT2 CASA-derived FFT2D -> FFTW Same whole-plane in-place strategy, with surrounding shift/normalization work. LibRA HPG CPU / CUDA fftw[f]_plan_many_dft / cufftPlanMany, rank 2 Explicit strides and batches; in-place/out-of-place kernels. CUDA uses cufftExecC2C or cufftExecZ2Z. The inspected kernels create/destroy plans per kernel call; do not claim universal persistent plan caching.

docs.title: CASA
docs.text:
Local repository: /Users/brianglendenning/SoftwareProjects/casa, HEAD 61020062cee290f5466cffed5ec5032e0c7a3434. Upstream: NRAO CASA6. Paths below are relative to casatools/src/code/:

  • synthesis/TransformMachines2/GridFT.cc: ft_p.c2cFFT at the model-to-grid and grid-to-image boundaries. This file has local diagnostic modifications; the same FFT call sites were verified in git show HEAD:....
  • synthesis/Utilities/FFT2D.h:46: FFTW is the constructor default.
  • synthesis/Utilities/FFT2D.cc:54-64: FFTW float/double thread initialization; thread count follows host/OpenMP configuration, not an unconditional one.
  • FFT2D.cc:349-431: centered transform, cached forward/backward rank-2 plans, FFTW_ESTIMATE, direct in-place array pointers and new-array execution.
  • FFT2D.cc:500-550: explicit quadrant swaps using a quarter-plane temporary; inverse normalization is combined with that operation. FFTW does not remove these application-level passes.
  • synthesis/MeasurementEquations/LatConvEquation.h: owns a LatticeConvolver<Float>; Clark's residual calculation calls its equation.

CASA's bundled casacore source is at /Users/brianglendenning/SoftwareProjects/casa/casatools/casacore, HEAD 25b653f6963a78a1dcfc8e16954081e091a50fbe:

  • lattices/LatticeMath/LatticeConvolver.tcc:178-245: reduced first Fourier axis, real-to-complex transform, spectrum multiplication and inverse.
  • lattices/LatticeMath/LatticeFFT.tcc:49-77: complex-plane transform when memory permits, otherwise line-by-line traversal. Its real-transform path also iterates axes/lines through FFTServer.
  • scimath/Mathematics/FFTServer.hcc:260-297: copies complex input into itsWorkC2C, invokes FFTW, normalizes inverse output and copies back. Lines 36-38 document removal of its FFTPACK alternative in 2020. Do not infer current generic FFTServer uses FFTPACK from older documentation.

The inspected FFT2D and casacore files are unmodified locally. CASA has multiple FFT users; the direct GridFT path must not be generalized to every utility or minor-cycle convolution.

docs.title: Obit
docs.text:
Pinned source: ObitFFT.c and ObitUVGrid.c. Inspected local build source: /Users/brianglendenning/SoftwareProjects/casa-rs-evidence/t55/obit-build/ebc1c229e5e3870b5ce3c342bddb7313d986a06f/core/src/.

  • ObitFFT.c:350-367, 490-494: direct single-precision FFTW execution on the array buffers for C2R and C2C.
  • ObitFFT.c:748-820: reverses the dimension list to reconcile column-major Obit arrays with FFTW's row-major interpretation, without transposing pixels; creates full 2D C2C/R2C/C2R plans with FFTW_ESTIMATE.
  • ObitUVGrid.c:722-725, 787-790: grid-to-real FFT followed by image centering.
  • ObitUVGrid.c:876-925: verifies the grid's first dimension is Nx/2+1, configures FFT threads, creates image/beam plans only when absent and executes them. The half-spectrum avoids storing the redundant half of a real image's Fourier representation; it is not a general substitution for complex images.
  • The file retains compile-time FFTW2/GSL alternatives. The existing local reference build's REFERENCE.md:73 records FFTW3f 3.3.11. No additional Obit installation or timing was performed.

docs.text:
Local repository: /Users/brianglendenning/SoftwareProjects/libRA, HEAD 0ab99e261878334d6588eafa360cef3b673e897f, local-fork revision, upstream. src/synthesis/Utilities/FFT2D.cc is unmodified and contains the same rank-2 FFTW strategy described above; TransformMachines2/GridFT.cc calls it. Older TransformMachines/GridFT.cc retains LatticeFFT calls.

HPG dependency: /Users/brianglendenning/SoftwareProjects/libRA/dependencies/HPG, HEAD 79667f64746425eb3cf34c3b83081e1af19df3db, pinned FFT source. The inspected include/hpg/fft.hpp is unmodified:

  • Lines 70-212: single/double FFTW execution and batched planning adapters.
  • Lines 218-288: rank-2 batched CPU planning with explicit strides/layout, FFTW_ESTIMATE | FFTW_PRESERVE_INPUT, execution and plan destruction.
  • Lines 342-434: float/double cuFFT execution, rank-2 cufftPlanMany, CUDA stream association and in-place execution. This is an available CUDA backend, not evidence that the local macOS build executes GPU FFTs.

docs.title: Implication for casa-rs
docs.text: A thin FFT adapter is normal and useful. The avoidable mechanism is our own repeated lane gathering/scattering around a 1D library, not the existence of a wrapper itself. Direct library-owned multidimensional transforms are the relevant CPU experiment. Obit's reduced Hermitian representation is another memory/work lesson for genuinely real transforms; adopting it would require checking the particular operator's semantics rather than assuming all grids are Hermitian. Do not reproduce CASA's older work-buffer copies merely for implementation similarity. No backend replacement, speedup or scientific acceptance is claimed by this research.

docs.title: Licensing clarification
docs.text:
Checked 2026-09-26. The owner, formerly responsible for the principal authors of CASA, Obit and LibRA, confirms none relies on a private FFTW licensing arrangement. There is no need to pursue that hypothesis.

FFTW is GPL-2.0-or-later. The relevant source headers provide a public-license route:

  • CASA synthesis/Utilities/FFT2D.cc:1-17 is GPL-2.0-or-later. CASA also contains LGPL components: its Python package LICENSE.txt contains Library GPL v2, and casacore's FFTW adapter is Library-GPL-2.0-or-later. A package label is not a complete license inventory of the linked imaging stack.
  • Obit core/LICENSE supplies GPLv2, and core/src/ObitFFT.c:1-20 explicitly grants GPLv2 or any later version.
  • LibRA's src/synthesis/Utilities/FFT2D.cc:1-17 and TransformMachines2/GridFT.cc:1-17 retain GPL-2.0-or-later grants. HPG's own LICENSE.spdx and FFT header identify Apache-2.0. That grant does not replace FFTW's license. Apache-2.0 and GPLv3 are compatible; Apache-2.0 is not compatible with GPLv2-only (Apache's explanation). The GPL components' later-version permission provides the relevant GPLv3 combination route.

Under the FSF's stated interpretation, a distributed program linked with a GPL library must satisfy GPL terms for the combined work, including applicable source, notices and license duties. Individual compatible components can retain their original source licenses; this is not automatic relicensing of every independent file or package. Dynamic linking or an LGPL/permissively licensed wrapper is not an exemption from the GPL dependency's terms.

casa-rs currently declares LGPL-3.0-or-later in workspace Cargo.toml. A GPLv3-compliant FFTW-linked distribution is a viable route, subject to checking the actual release's complete dependency set and packaging. Independent casa-rs components can retain LGPL source licensing, but a downstream consumer cannot treat the FFTW-linked combination as LGPL-only with unrestricted proprietary-linking permission. No paid FFTW license is needed merely to develop, benchmark, or distribute a GPL-compliant build. Preserving LGPL-only downstream linking flexibility for that same FFTW-linked product would require another licensing solution or a different backend.

This is an engineering reading of published terms, not a legal opinion or a compliance audit of any project's release artifacts. No casa-rs license, dependency, or distribution policy was changed. NVIDIA cuFFT has separate terms; this clarification concerns the FFTW CPU paths, not a CUDA distribution audit.

docs.title: Imaging foundation: review and phased refactor plan
docs.text: Truth class: normative plan Date: 2026-10-07 Branch: claude/imaging-foundation (cut from codex/t55-full-size-validation at e714fd2339) Status: APPROVED by the owner on 2026-10-07 (decisions D1–D10 and closure of the #486 family included). COMPLETE: IF-0 to IF-11 landed by 2026-10-16. Section 5 states the landed signatures (IF-11, #660), and the deviations the tickets took are reconciled into sections 3 and 5 (section 12). Reviewed sources: six read-only deep dives over the imaging crates, the RadioAstronomyOracle corpus (NRAO 2024/2026 synthesis workshop slides, Synthesis Imaging II), CASA synthesis/ C++, LibRA/HPG, and issues #486,

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
Review the cube, MFS, Clark, multi-worker and Metal imaging code added under programme #486 and define one refactor that leaves a single mathematical imaging foundation. After it, standard, W-projection, AW-projection, mosaic, MT-MFS, cube and MFS imaging are parameterisations of one measurement operator, one major-cycle pass, one deconvolution driver and one execution model, on CPU or Metal. Performance and memory stay within the measured checkpoints. Code that exists only to re-verify, re-hash, re-validate or re-describe what the type system or an earlier layer already guarantees is removed.

This document is written so that a different implementer (Opus) can execute each ticket from the text without re-deriving the design. Where a signature is given, it is the intended signature. Where a file is named for deletion, the ticket is not done until the file is gone.

Section 2 records owner decisions already made. Section 3 lists decisions this plan asks the owner to confirm. Section 4 is the review. Sections 5 to 8 are the design, deletion list and test strategy. Section 9 is the ticket set with the review gates. Section 10 is the anti-slop rule set every ticket is reviewed against. Section 11 is process.

docs.title: 2. Owner decisions recorded 2026-10-07
docs.text:
• Base: branch from the T55 tip, not main. T55 stays unmerged; the first merged ticket of this plan carries its content to main.
  • Plan first, then tickets. Opus implements most tickets; Fable lands the foundation tickets (IF-0, IF-1) so later tickets have a concrete pattern.
  • Breadth first: convert all imaging code to the shared design using tests that take at most about ten minutes each, then run one systematic performance and memory pass against the representative datasets.
  • Shrink runtime bookkeeping (receipts, evidence, ledgers, resource authority) to what admission, cancellation, Metal fences, bounded streaming and atomic publication need. ADR text is superseded where required.
  • Move mosaic, W and AW onto the shared operator now and thoroughly, so no second refactor follows.
  • Prefer fewer law-based tests over fixture-heavy tests. Each guaranteed behaviour keeps coverage; the count of tests is not a goal.
  • Programme #486 and its subsidiary tickets may be closed as superseded, with a new ticket set, provided no work or evidence is lost.
  • Resource limits: 16 GiB native, two Cargo jobs. GLENDENNING is mounted; CASA is at /opt/homebrew/bin/casa.
  • Review gates: at logical points the owner has Fable and (probably) OpenAI Astra review the implementation for drift from these goals and replan from discoveries. Section 9.3 defines them.
  • D2 agreed, with the addition that CPU f32 grids are a user-selectable switch for large problems. Obit and LibRA are to be surveyed for processing techniques worth adopting; adopted ones are recorded in section 5.9.

docs.title: 3. Decisions requested from the owner
docs.text:
Each is stated with the recommendation. Approval of the plan approves these unless the owner strikes one.

  • D1 Replay cache. Delete the gridded-normal replay subsystem (gridded_normal_operator*, complete_data_operator.rs, metal_normal.rs, the replay half of managed_spill.rs; about 20k lines). Later major cycles re-traverse the MeasurementSet and grid V − A·m per sample, as CASA does. Reason: the cache is not scientifically required; it stores about 40 bytes per row-channel sample, which for the Wave3 workload is an 86 GB scratch reservation against a 36 GB input; it is valid only while weighting is frozen; and it forms the residual as a difference of two large f64 images rather than gridding the residual visibilities. The performance pass (IF-10) may add a bounded tap-plan cache as an execution strategy over the same operator if measurement shows it pays. Qualified (#659 deviation 7, owner 2026-10-14): a run keeps its samples' imaging weights, not the samples, across passes (WeightCache, 4 bytes a selected row and channel) when it has one image domain, a constant or Taylor basis and every plane resident, and the slots fit a sixteenth of the free memory; they are admitted before they are allocated. A record or placement cache across majors (2.6–8.9 GB a major on the 32-channel cube) stays rejected.
  • D2 Grid precision (owner agreed 2026-10-07). Metal is one implementation of the backend trait and accumulates in f32 with atomic adds (nondeterministic order). The CPU accumulates in f64 by default. This is consistent with the owner's 2026-09-24 numerical direction: acceptance is the 1e-3 normalised tolerance, not bitwise agreement. Grid precision is a user-selectable request field, gridprecision = auto | f32 | f64, exposed in the parameter catalog. auto selects f64 for constant and Taylor bases on CPU and f32 for channel-local cubes and for Metal. f32 halves grid and accumulator memory so large problems become tractable on this workstation; the CPU backend supports both precisions for every convolution-function set. Amended by the owner 2026-10-15 (#659): auto selects f64 on the CPU for every basis, channel-local cubes included, and f32 on Metal. An f32 running sum drifts with the number of samples a grid cell takes: a mosaic cube's weight image, which takes every sample of a channel at the uv origin, missed CASA (which accumulates in double) by 2.6e-3. f32 stays a user choice for large problems, and choosing the GPU accepts it. Device choice (#659 deviation 14, owner 2026-10-15): backend = auto | cpu | gpu, defaulting to auto, which takes Metal only for problems a T1 Metal law compares with the CPU (section 5.8); an explicit gridprecision = f64 keeps auto on the CPU.
  • D3 AW convolution-function cache. Replace the private content-addressed prepared-artifact store (manifest schema 7, 18 hash domains, eviction ledger; about 15k lines across aw_cache.rs, prepared_aw_phase.rs, prepared_artifact*) with: read CASA CFS_*/WTCFS_* images directly into an in-memory LRU of cells; native EVLA CF generation writes CASA-format CF images into a cache directory, so one loader serves both. Payload checksums on an importable, regenerable cache are dropped.
  • D4 Crate layout. Split casa-imaging-reconstruction into casa-imaging-operator (measurement operator, convolution functions, weighting, normal images) and casa-imaging-deconvolution (minor-cycle driver, solvers, PSF summary, masks). Add casa-imaging-metal (macOS only) implementing the backend trait. Move the CASA image writer into casa-imaging-products. Delete casa-imaging-reconstruction when empty. As landed (IF-11, #660 deviation 1): the operator owns the NormalImages a pass finishes into and CASA's continuum fit; the normal state the minor cycle and products read (resident or paged), the model lifecycle and its storage seam, the masks and the MajorCycle that pairs model and normal state went to deconvolution, because the masks read the normal state and the lifecycle uses the masks' reprojection. The reconstruction crate was deleted in IF-11.
  • D5 Runtime core. Replace receipts (schema 25), the execution DAG, execution bindings, the resource-authority topology, observation transactions and the cost model with: HostResources, one admit() per phase returning an RAII reservation, a sequential phase list with a cancel token, the trimmed Metal execution state, the bounded worker team, and an O(1)-per-phase RunSummary. ADR-0010 is superseded by a new ADR-0016. Extended (#659 deviation 8, owner 2026-10-15): the policy returns a core allocation (ResourcePolicy::cores): compute workers for minor cycles and products, and streaming workers for passes, as many as fit beside the source's producer thread within the policy's core budget. A run holds two worker teams (WorkerTeams), one pool when the widths agree.
  • D6 Architecture checker. Retire scripts/check-imaging-architecture.py (3,578 lines; hashes Rust function bodies and pins four SHA-256 ratchets), test-imaging-architecture-structural.py, migration-matrix.json, baselines/ and the representative-science receipt registry. Replace with a dependency-direction check (about 150 lines) over cargo metadata plus a forbidden-import grep (device APIs only in casa-imaging-metal; no std::env in library crates; no sha2/crc in imaging crates outside external-format readers).
  • D7 Programme closure. Close #486 and T-tickets #541, #543, #546, #552, #553, #554 as superseded by the IF ticket set, each with a closing comment that links this plan, the final T55 commit, the durable evidence roots on GLENDENNING and the NAS, and the IF ticket that inherits its outcome. #625 closes into IF-10 (its serial AW/MT-MFS time bar becomes an IF-10 acceptance row). #341 closes into IF-5; #217 into IF-8. The VLASS wave #445–#450 stays open with a comment that IF-3/IF-10 are its route.
  • D8 Request layer. One ImagingRequest serde struct, defaulted and validated from the provider-contracts catalog, replaces CliConfig, ImagerRunTaskRequest's mirror types, ContinuumImagingRequest and ApplicationRequest. Dead and always-rejected task requirements are removed from the catalog, not merely from the Rust enum.
  • D9 Diagnostics. Library crates read no environment variables. Diagnostic switches become fields of ImagingRequest.diagnostics (stage timing, Metal stage profiling, science trace); everything is emitted through tracing via casa-logging. The required CASA_RS_IMAGING_SPILL_*_BYTES_PER_SECOND variables and the same-filesystem requirement disappear with the cost model.
  • D10 Cube state paging. Keep one paged cube-state implementation (managed_cube_blocks + managed_model/managed_normal); delete paged_cube_state.rs.

docs.title: 4.1 Shape of the code today
docs.text:
Imaging source (non-test) is about 200k lines across six crates; tests add about 65k. Twenty-two files exceed 3,000 lines; spectral_operator.rs is 15,182 lines and receipt.rs is 8,455.

The runtime split is not cube versus MFS. It is a fast cube path (BulkCubePhase: natural weighting, no start model, no visibility transform, one SPW/field/polarisation layout, CPU gridding loop in reconstruction/src/streaming_cube/band.rs) versus a general path (SpectralCycleExecutor) serving MFS, MT-MFS, Briggs/uniform cubes, mosaic and any MODEL_DATA write. Both plug into one application-level MajorCyclePhase loop (application/src/lib.rs:404-864) and converge on run_reconstruction_cycle (runtime/src/spectral_cycle.rs:3357).

Four CPU drivers implement the same grid/degrid mathematics:

Driver Lines Capabilities cube band loop streaming_cube/band.rs 1,712 standard CF, natural weighting, f32 grids, one SPW layout SpectralSlabOperator in spectral_operator.rs:7542-10871 ~3,300 standard, W, AW, mosaic via enum match; sample-serial on one f64 grid; a Mutex per AW sample gridded-normal replay gridded_normal_operator* + runtime complete_data_operator.rs + managed_spill.rs ~11,300 + 6,400 + 4,200 residual major cycles over spilled 40-byte records; fixed 4+4 logical lanes; six record layouts; a legacy sector path compiled only under cfg(test) initial MFS planes spectral_operator/initial_planes* ~1,100 initial pass with empty model only; 64-row strips

Metal has two more drivers (streaming_cube/metal_wave.rs 1,068 and complete_data_operator/metal_normal.rs 647) over one runtime (metal_runtime.rs 3,113) with six MSL kernels in one inline string (metal_cube.rs:19-268). The kernels hard-code seven separable real taps and oversampling 100, accumulate with relaxed f32 atomics, and re-implement the CPU row interpolation and Stokes reduction in MSL. Three double-buffer ticket rings and two arena layout schemes are duplicated across the drivers. FFTs are FFTW everywhere; CLEAN, normalisation and publication are CPU.

Gridders are closed enums (ConvolutionOperator{Standard,WProjection}, OperatorTaps{Standard,Aw,Mosaic}) matched at about twenty sites. AW (aw_projection.rs 3,137) and mosaic (mosaic.rs 1,593) are separate code paths that neither the fast cube path nor the Metal kernels can use. CASA's linear channel resampling is implemented five times; the Stokes-I reducer four times; the standard seven-tap loop six times; model FFT preparation and image formation twice each; seven different per-sample transport structs exist.

Clark is one implementation (minor_cycle/clark.rs) with sparse and FFT refresh. But one dispatch (run_reconstruction_cycle) feeds four separate CLEAN loops (per-plane Hogbom/Clark/multiscale, image-domain Hogbom, Taylor, joint) with four copies of the threshold formula, four of mask validation and three of evidence minting. Peak search exists at about nine sites and PSF subtraction at about eight. The Taylor and joint candidate selectors are about 80% identical. The circular residual refreshes are O(iterations × samples × N²) where an FFT refresh exists already. Clark's sparse refresh spawns raw std::thread::scope threads outside the worker team. Known inconsistencies: Clark admits peaks at or below threshold where the others require strictly below; the 1% global-convergence check runs only for single-plane and Taylor runs; divergence tests differ per solver; and the multi-plane cycle-threshold prepass filters the residual by mask only while the in-solve peak uses mask plus valid support, which changes the shared threshold in PB-limited fields.

docs.title: 4.2 Bookkeeping and process machinery
docs.text:
• Execution is sequential: run_inner starts no threads; next_action dispatches the first ready DAG node in id order. Parallelism exists only inside a node (FixedWorkerTeam) plus asynchronous Metal/IO fences. A Hogbom run with N major cycles builds N+2 plans, each admitted, run, receipted and reopened.
  • Receipts are write-only. The single production read is the planned worker count, which the plan already holds. Each phase reopens its receipt, which does a payload SHA-256, about 86 integrity checks and a full DAG rebuild and rehash. receipt.rs (8,316 production lines) defines about fifty projection structs. External readers: one manual tool (tools/perf/imager/intermediate_profile_evidence.py). The Mac app, TUI and casars-imager read none.
  • Admission happens twice (plan() acquires and releases a lease; the scheduler acquires again). Host memory is layered at least eight times over one number. "Preferred" is always set equal to "hard". About 120 budget/claim-style type names exist. The time prediction that orders worker candidates is a constant 1 ms per stage, so the search is a sort by node count. cost_model.rs (804 lines) is only ever bootstrapped.
  • Cancellation is not wired: the controller returns Continue or Adapt; there is no SIGINT handler. The low-memory adaptation is unreachable from casars-imager.
  • ADR-0015 violation on the hot path: bounded_stream.rs finalises a SHA-256 per partition per worker, then per block, then per window (:863-1370); nothing reads them but eprintln! and tests.
  • Probable bug: attempt ids are deterministic over paths, image size, cell and phase centre; begin() refuses an existing receipt, so re-running into the same image name should fail until retention prunes the old receipt. It goes away with receipts.
  • Native runs require two environment variables for storage rates and that input and output share a filesystem.
  • About 163 distinct CASA_RS_* names exist; 12 are read in production (section 8.3). There are about 120 production eprintln! sites. No imaging crate depends on tracing although casa-logging exists.
  • Request parameters are carried by eight struct types between the command line and CompiledProblem; specmode has seven spellings; AW controls have five. Defaults drifted between the CLI and JSON paths (gridder, write_preview_pngs). task_contract.rs (5,033 lines) is about 65% mirror types, restated defaults and their round-trip tests; its progress schema is emitted by no Rust code. Of 38 TaskRequirement variants, 21 are dead or always rejected, and 12 catalog parameters exist only to be rejected when set. JointContinuumLine is unreachable. About 1,950 lines compute SHA-256 identities over contracts that are only compared with themselves in one process. The selected-row sequence is re-hashed per sample in production.
  • Three tests on the T55 branch have stale fixture budgets after T55's accounting changes (issue #541, 2026-10-06 comment).
  • scripts/check-imaging-architecture.py hashes Rust function bodies and struct fields and pins four SHA-256 ratchets over a 115 KB migration matrix (77 rows, contract revision 93). It would fight every commit of this refactor. ADR-0009's dependency-direction rule is the only part to keep.
  • Representative-science evidence: 18 of 19 matrix rows have lost their external CASA receipts (--require-external fails), so T2 oracles must be regenerated during IF-10. scripts/test-imaging-parity.sh runs a deleted test binary.

docs.title: 4.3 What is worth keeping
docs.text:
• ADR-0009's mathematical contract (A, A, W, H = AWA, paired operators, spectral law/sampling/basis/coupling, product contract). The refactor implements it rather than replacing it.
  • The CPU seven-tap kernel maths, the W-plane kernel construction, the AW cell selection rules (conjugate frequency, Mueller swap on w sign, pointing phasor, division by norm on degrid only), the mosaic PB-phased kernels and the density-weighting cell rules. These are CASA-pinned science and are moved, not rewritten.
  • One Clark implementation with sparse and FFT refresh; the half-spectrum RealFft2<f32> refresh.
  • FixedWorkerTeam, execute_bounded/execute_overlapped and the one or two slot producer/consumer stream in bounded_stream.rs, without measurements and digests.
  • MetalExecutionState device, queue, buffer residency, submit/wait/drain.
  • The managed spill v4 framed writer/reader (same-run, no CRC) for cube inputs; one paged cube-state backend.
  • Atomic individual-image replacement in casa_product_sink.rs.
  • generate_synthetic_observation_ms in casa-ms (analytic point and Gaussian skies, multiple pointings, full polarisation; extended to several spectral windows in IF-0).
  • The CASA comparison tooling (tools/perf/imager/perf_harness/image_compare.py, tolerances.py, run_workload.py, mfs_4096_pilot.py), the golden datasets on GLENDENNING and the NAS archive.
  • Measured checkpoints as the acceptance bars for IF-10: cube Metal W4 deep32 109.95 s; MFS intermediate-90 four-SPW pilot CPU W1 29.80 s / W4 15.82 s / Metal W4 14.80 s versus CASA 52.82 s; MFS 512-channel 512² W1 48.46 s / W4 20.25 s; C-array 512-channel cube CASA 6.0 h; Wave3 4096² MFS CASA 7,268 s.

docs.title: 5.1 Formalism (normative vocabulary for code and docs)
docs.text:
Per baseline, frequency ν and time, the measurement equation is

V_ij(ν,t) = M_ij · S · ∬ M^S_ij(l,m,ν,t) I(l,m,ν) e^{-2πi(ul+vm+w(n-1))} dl dm / n

with M_ij direction-independent gains (calibration, outside imaging), M^S_ij the direction-dependent Mueller response (primary beam, parallactic angle, leakage), and w(n−1) the w-term. Let x be the model coefficients on the pixel grid and d the selected unweighted visibility samples. The forward operator A : X → D and its adjoint A* are composed as

A   = Degrid ∘ Fft ∘ Correction ∘ PolBasis⁻¹ ∘ ModelPrescale   (R1: the same diagonal 1/grdsf on both sides, CASA GridFT)
A*  = PolBasis ∘ Correction ∘ Fft⁻¹ ∘ Grid
W   = diag(input weight · taper · density weight), flags removed from D
b   = A* W d          dirty image (unnormalised)
H   = A* W A          normal operator; PSF = A* W 1
g(x)= A* W (d − A x)  residual image, formed by gridding residual samples
sumwt(plane,pol) = Σ W  (AW: Σ W·|Σ taps|)

Capability-specific factors and the per-sample data they need:

Capability What changes Per-sample / per-row data Standard kernel = prolate spheroidal, real, separable, support 3, oversampling 100 u,v,w,ν, weight, flag, polarisation W-projection kernel = C ⋆ FT[e^{2πi w(√(1−l²−m²)−1)}] per w-plane; complex; support grows with w A-projection kernel = FT[A_i ⊗ A_j*]; image divided by PB response afterwards PA cell, antenna-type pair, frequency cell, Mueller row AW (wideband) both; conjugate-beam frequency √(2ν0²−ν²) when conjbeams w, PA, frequency, Mueller, pointing phase gradient Mosaic kernel = FT[PB] with phase ramp e^{2πi(uΔl_k+vΔm_k)}; weight image from FT[PB²] per-row pointing offset → phase gradient MT-MFS A_t = A·diag(((ν−ν0)/ν0)^t); 2N_t−1 PSFs, N_t residuals per-sample spectral factor s = (ν−ν0)/ν0 Cube same A per plane; chanMap routes samples to planes plane index Stokes/Mueller polMap correlation → grid pol; Mueller row maps swap between forward and adjoint Mueller row per direction

Paired (same choice in forward and adjoint, ADR-0009): the kernel set, support and oversampling; the gridding correction; the conjugation convention (w sign, Mueller row swap); the phase gradient (ramp vs conj ramp); the phase-centre phasor; chanMap/polMap; Taylor factors; the FT[PB]/FT[PB²] pair. Data-only: flags, W, density weights, sumwt. Image-only, owned by the product contract and never folded into A*: PB normalisation (flatnoise, flatsky, pbsquare), pblimit blanking, restoring beam, pbcor. CASA's normalisation conventions are tabulated in section 5.7 and are the acceptance reference.
